mainTopic: Laws of the אבל: standing for קריעה, the ban on Torah learning and its exception for teaching the public, and when a mourner may wear תפילין
overview: This amud opens by asking whether a mourner must stand when doing קריעה. A challenge comparing קריעה to חליצה is answered by looking at how each פסוק is worded. רמי בר חמא brings a proof from איוב, but the גמרא pushes back that איוב may have done more than he had to. A proof from דוד המלך meets the same pushback, until a ברייתא and the answer 'כעין ארצה' show that דוד only lay on his overturned bed, so that proof stands. The גמרא then lists what an אבל may not do, including all Torah learning. The exception is that he may teach if the public needs him, but without setting up his own תורגמן. Finally, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about when an אבל may put on תפילין, and each side's פסוק is explained. עולא rules partly like each one, and the amud ends with a challenge to רבא that is answered on the next amud.

steps.title: Challenge from חליצה: does 'standing' in a verse really require standing?
steps.stepSummary: If a word like 'stood' in a פסוק requires standing, then חליצה should require standing too. But a ברייתא says חליצה can be done sitting, standing, or reclining.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, the פסוק about חליצה says 'And he stands and says: I do not wish to take her.' Must he stand here too? But a ברייתא teaches: whether sitting, whether standing, whether reclining!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the idea that קריעה must be done standing just because a פסוק says 'he arose and tore.' He points to חליצה, where the פסוק also mentions standing, yet standing is not required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic being attacked is: 'the פסוק mentions standing, so standing is required.' The same logic would make standing required for חליצה. A ברייתא openly says חליצה works in any position, so that logic seems broken.

keyTerms.meaning: But now, if so (introduces a challenge that pushes a reasoning to an unacceptable result)
The ceremony that frees a יבמה from marrying her late husband's brother
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But now, if that is so:
"And he stands and says: I do not wish to take her,"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:8. This is the brother's line in the חליצה ceremony.

phrases.english: here too [must he stand]?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יוֹשֵׁב בֵּין עוֹמֵד בֵּין מוּטֶּה!
phrases.english: whether sitting, whether standing, whether reclining!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim, made just before this section, that 'ויקם ויקרע' requires standing for קריעה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that a verse mentioning standing makes standing required for קריעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חליצה verse also mentions standing, yet a ברייתא says standing is not required there. So mentioning standing does not prove a requirement.

steps.title: The answer: the wording of the two verses is different
steps.stepSummary: The חליצה verse does not say 'he shall stand and say' as an instruction. The קריעה verse does say 'he arose and tore,' linking the standing to the tearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There it is not written 'and he shall stand and he shall say.' Here it is written 'and he arose and tore.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer separates the two cases by looking closely at how each פסוק is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חליצה, 'ועמד' is just part of describing the case, not a command to stand while speaking. By איוב, the פסוק ties the rising directly to the tearing: 'ויקם... ויקרע.' So the standing is part of the act of קריעה, and the challenge does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Here (the case we are discussing, קריעה)

phrases.english: He said to him:
There it is not written "and he shall stand and he shall say,"
here it is written "and he arose and tore."
phrases.notes: איוב 1:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חליצה challenge from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases based on the wording of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any verse that mentions standing creates a requirement to stand, so חליצה and קריעה should be the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only where the verse links the standing to the act itself, as in 'ויקם ויקרע,' is standing required. חליצה has no such link.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: קריעה is done standing, learned from איוב
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks where we learn that קריעה must be done standing, and answers from the פסוק 'ויקם איוב ויקרע.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: From where do we know that קריעה is done standing? As it says: 'And איוב arose and tore.'
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא states a rule, that קריעה must be done standing, and gives a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof is that איוב stood up and then tore his garment, so standing is part of how קריעה is done. The next step will test whether this proof really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Tearing one's garment as a sign of mourning
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: רמי בר חמא said:
From where do we know that tearing is done standing?
As it is said: "And איוב arose and tore."
phrases.notes: איוב 1:20

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: מִנַּיִן לִקְרִיעָה שֶׁהִיא מְעוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new source discussion: what is the source for standing during קריעה?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קריעה must be done standing, as learned from 'ויקם איוב ויקרע.'

steps.title: Pushback: maybe איוב did more than he had to
steps.stepSummary: Maybe איוב's standing was something extra, beyond the basic requirement. After all, the same פסוק says he shaved his head, and that is surely not required of every mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he did something extra? For if you do not say so, then 'and he shaved his head': must everyone do that too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רמי בר חמא's proof. Not everything איוב did is required of every mourner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says איוב shaved his head, and nobody holds that every mourner must shave his head. So איוב clearly did extra things, and standing might be one of them. That means the proof from איוב is not strong enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra thing, beyond what is required
For if you do not say so

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying standing is NOT required. It only says this particular פסוק cannot prove it, because איוב may have done more than the minimum.

phrases.english: Perhaps it was an extra thing that he did?
For if you do not say so,
"and he shaved his head": must [everyone do] so too?
phrases.notes: These words come right after 'ויקרע' in the same פסוק, איוב 1:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from איוב given in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from איוב, not the rule that קריעה is done standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: איוב's actions included extras, like shaving his head, so his standing may also have been extra and not a requirement.

steps.title: A new proof: דוד המלך stood and tore
steps.stepSummary: Since the proof from איוב failed, the גמרא brings a different פסוק: 'ויקם המלך ויקרע את בגדיו.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from here: 'And the king arose and tore his garments.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the איוב proof and offers a new source from דוד's mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק shows the same pattern, rising and then tearing, but from a different person. The hope is that this source avoids the problem of 'maybe he did extra.'

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And the king arose and tore his garments."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 13:31. This is דוד המלך, mourning his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from step 3 with a new פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That קריעה must be done standing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 13:31, 'ויקם המלך ויקרע את בגדיו.'

steps.title: The same pushback: maybe דוד also did extra
steps.stepSummary: Maybe דוד's standing was also extra. The same פסוק says he lay on the ground, and that is not required of every mourner.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he did something extra? For if you do not say so, then 'and he lay on the ground': must everyone do that too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same objection against the new proof from דוד. Step 7 backs this up, and step 8 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like איוב shaving his head, דוד lying on the ground is not something every mourner must do. So this פסוק also shows a mourner doing extra things, and standing could be one of them. The proof from דוד is now weakened in the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: And he lay on the ground

steps.whatToRemember: Two proofs that קריעה is done standing, from איוב and from דוד, both face the same problem: the mourner in the פסוק also did extra things that are not required. Step 8 rescues the proof from דוד.

phrases.english: But perhaps he did an extra thing?
For if you do not say so,
"and he lay on the ground": must [everyone do] so too?
phrases.notes: These words are from the same פסוק about דוד, שמואל ב 13:31.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same objection as step 4 against the new proof from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from דוד, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: דוד also did something extra, lying on the ground, so his standing may also have been beyond the requirement.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows lying on the ground is not required of a mourner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its push-back. A ברייתא says a mourner who sits even on the ground has not fulfilled his duty, because he did not do כפיית המטה. So lying on the ground is clearly not required, and דוד did something extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if a mourner sat on a bed, a chair, a large mortar, or the ground, he did not fulfill his duty with any of them. רבי יוחנן explained: this is because he did not overturn his bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens the push-back from step 6. A ברייתא shows that lying on the ground is not a mourner's duty at all, so דוד's lying on the ground was something extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says even sitting on the ground does not count, because the real duty is כפיית המטה. So lying on the ground cannot be a requirement, and דוד's lying on the ground must have been extra. That makes it more likely his standing was extra too. Step 8 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: A large mortar, a heavy stone or wooden bowl used for grinding
Overturning the bed, a mourner's duty

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: if he sat on a bed,
on a chair,
on a large mortar,
or on the ground,
with none of them has he fulfilled his obligation.
And רבי יוחנן said:
Because he did not fulfill the overturning of the bed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the push-back of step 6 by proving that lying on the ground is not required
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from דוד in step 5, that standing for קריעה is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says sitting on the ground does not fulfill mourning, since the duty is כפיית המטה. So lying on the ground is not required, דוד did extra, and his standing may be extra too.

steps.title: דוד was only close to the ground, on his overturned bed
steps.stepSummary: The answer: 'ארצה' means 'like on the ground.' דוד lay on his overturned bed, which is close to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it means something like on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. דוד did not lie on the bare ground; he lay on his overturned bed, which brought him close to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now דוד's 'lying on the ground' was simply the normal mourner's duty of כפיית המטה, not something extra. That cancels the push-back in step 6. So the proof from דוד's פסוק comes back: קריעה is done standing.

keyTerms.meaning: To the ground (the word in the פסוק about דוד)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'ויקם המלך ויקרע' stands as the source that קריעה is done standing, because דוד's 'lying on the ground' was only his overturned bed.

phrases.english: He said to him: it was like on the ground.
phrases.notes: The פסוק's word 'ארצה' means low, close to the ground, because his bed was turned over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push-back of steps 6-7 and so brings back the proof of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד lay on the bare ground, which mourners are not required to do, so his standing might also be extra
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד lay on his overturned bed, the normal duty, so his standing is also the normal requirement for קריעה

steps.title: What a mourner may not do, and the exception for teaching the public
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists things an אבל may not do: work, bathing, anointing, marital relations, wearing shoes, and learning Torah of all kinds. But if the public needs him to teach, he does not hold back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: these are the things a mourner may not do. He may not work, bathe, anoint himself, have marital relations, or wear shoes. He may not read תורה, נביאים or כתובים, or learn משנה, מדרש, הלכות, תלמוד or אגדות. But if the public needs him, he does not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא listing what an אבל may not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even Torah learning of every kind is on the list of things an אבל may not do. But there is an exception: if the community needs him to teach, he may teach. The next few steps build on that exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The public needs him, to teach them

steps.confusionAlert: Torah learning is on the forbidden list, even though it is a מצוה. The exception covers only teaching the public, not private learning.

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
These are the things a mourner is forbidden to do:
He is forbidden to work and to bathe,
to anoint himself, to have marital relations,
and to wear shoes.
And he is forbidden to read in the תורה,
in the נביאים, and in the כתובים,
and to learn משנה, מדרש, and הלכות,
and תלמוד and אגדות.
But if the public needs him,
he does not hold back.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, וְאֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָבֵל אָסוּר בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the list of things forbidden to a mourner
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל may not work, bathe, anoint, have relations, wear shoes, or learn Torah, but he may teach if the public needs him

steps.title: רבי יוסי taught all day after his son died
steps.stepSummary: A story supports the exception: when רבי יוסי's son died in ציפורי, he went into the בית המדרש and taught the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story: רבי יוסי's son died in ציפורי, and he went into the בית המדרש and taught the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a story to back up the exception it just stated. A great sage taught the public on the very day his son died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the exception in real life. A mourner whom the public needs may teach, even on the first day of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught publicly, gave a lecture

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּצִיפּוֹרִי,
phrases.english: And there was a story: רבי יוסי's son died in ציפורי,
and he went into the study hall,
and taught the entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּצִיפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the exception at the end of step 9 with a story
steps.raayaObject: A mourner the public needs may teach
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוסי teaching all day after his son died in ציפורי

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה is told to give his lecture while mourning
steps.stepSummary: A death happened in רבה בר בר חנה's family, and he planned not to give his public lecture. רבי חנינא told him the rule: if the public needs him, he does not hold back.
steps.simpleTranslation: A death happened in רבה בר בר חנה's family, and he thought not to go out to give his lecture. רבי חנינא said to him: if the public needs him, he does not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where the exception from the ברייתא is put into practice. רבי חנינא tells a mourning sage to go teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר בר חנה thought the mourning rules kept him from teaching. רבי חנינא quoted the ברייתא's exception, so he was allowed, and expected, to give his lecture. This sets up the next step, where a limit is added.

keyTerms.meaning: Something bad happened to him (a gentle way of saying someone in his family died)

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיתְּרַעָא בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא,
phrases.english: Something bad happened to רבה בר בר חנה,
phrases.notes: This is a gentle way of saying someone in his family died.

phrases.english: and he thought not to go out to give the lecture.
רבי חנינא said to him:
If the public needs him,
he does not hold back.
phrases.notes: He is quoting the end of the ברייתא from step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אִיתְּרַעָא בֵּיהּ מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the exception from step 9 to a real case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourning sage whom the public needs should give his lecture

steps.title: A mourner may teach, but without a תורגמן
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה planned to set up an אמורא to repeat his words aloud, as usual. רב quoted a ברייתא: he may teach only if he does not set up a תורגמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought to set up an אמורא next to him. רב said to him: it is taught in a ברייתא, provided that he does not set up a תורגמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to the exception. A mourner may teach the public, but in a simpler way, without the usual speaker who repeats his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a big lecture had a תורגמן who called out the teacher's words to the crowd, which made the event grand. Since a mourner should not act in a festive way, רב says the mourner may teach but without that grand setup. So the exception is allowed, but in a toned-down form.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the speaker who repeats the teacher's words aloud to the crowd
The same speaker, one who calls out the teacher's words

steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may not learn Torah, but if the public needs him he may teach, only without a תורגמן.

phrases.english: He thought to set up an אמורא next to him.
phrases.notes: An אמורא here is the person who calls out the lecturer's words so the whole crowd can hear.

phrases.english: רב said to him: it is taught in a ברייתא,
provided that he does not set up a תורגמן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the exception that was applied in step 11
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A mourner whom the public needs may teach, but he may not set up a תורגמן to repeat his words

steps.title: So how can a mourner be heard?
steps.stepSummary: If an אבל may not set up a תורגמן, how does the crowd hear his lesson?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then how should he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question that sets up the next move: without a תורגמן, how does the mourner's lesson reach the crowd?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the אבל may teach only if he does not set up his own תורגמן. But a big crowd cannot hear a whisper, so the גמרא asks how this works in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he act? How should he do it?
The speaker who repeats the teacher's words out loud to the crowd

phrases.english: But then how does he do it?
phrases.notes: Since the mourner may not set up his own speaker, how can the crowd hear him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the rule from step 12 in practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a mourning teacher's words reach the public without his own תורגמן

steps.title: The whisper chain of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא story: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי whispered to רבי חנניה בן עקביא, who whispered to the תורגמן, who announced it to the crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The son of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי died, and he went into the בית המדרש. רבי חנניה בן עקביא came in and sat next to him. רבי יהודה whispered to רבי חנניה, רבי חנניה whispered to the תורגמן, and the תורגמן announced it to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a story showing the correct method. The mourner whispers to someone else, and that person passes it to the תורגמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mourner never speaks to the תורגמן himself, so he is not setting up his own תורגמן. The extra middle person changes the usual setup, and that change shows everyone he is in mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that really happened

phrases.english: Like that which is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַאי,
phrases.english: There was an incident: the son of רבי יהודה בר אילעאי died,
and he went into the study hall.

phrases.aramaic: וְנִכְנַס רַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא וְיָשַׁב בְּצִדּוֹ,
phrases.english: And רבי חנניה בן עקביא came in and sat beside him,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָחַשׁ הוּא לְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא,
phrases.english: and he (רבי יהודה) whispered to רבי חנניה בן עקביא,
and רבי חנניה בן עקביא whispered to the speaker,
phrases.notes: The word 'whispered' is left out here, but it carries over from the line before.

phrases.english: and the speaker announced it to the public.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's question with a story
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mourner whispers to a colleague, who passes it to the תורגמן, so the mourner never sets up his own תורגמן
steps.whatToRemember: An אבל may teach the public when needed, but not in the usual way: he whispers to a middle person, who passes it to the תורגמן.

steps.title: When may a mourner put on תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says an אבל may put on תפילין from the third day, and need not take them off for new visitors. רבי יהושע says from the second day, but he must take them off for new visitors.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A mourner may not put on תפילין during the first three days. From the third day on, including the third day, he may put them on. If new visitors come, he does not take them off. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: A mourner may not put on תפילין during the first two days. From the second day on, including the second day, he may put them on. If new visitors come, he takes them off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא with a מחלוקת about when an אבל may start wearing תפילין again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's no-תפילין time is longer (until the third day), but once he puts them on, he keeps them on even for new visitors. רבי יהושע allows them earlier (on the second day), but makes him remove them when new visitors come.

keyTerms.meaning: The leather boxes with פסוקים, worn during weekday prayer
New faces, visitors who had not yet come to comfort him

steps.confusionAlert: 'The first three days are forbidden' does not mean he waits until after the third day. The same line says that on the third day itself he may already put them on.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A mourner, during the first three days,
is forbidden to put on tefillin;
from the third day on, and the third day is included,
he is permitted to put on tefillin.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם בָּאוּ פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת — אֵינוֹ חוֹלֵץ,
phrases.english: And if new faces come, he does not take them off,
these are the words of רבי אליעזר.
רבי יהושע says:

phrases.aramaic: אָבֵל, שְׁנֵי יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים אָסוּר לְהַנִּיחַ תְּפִילִּין.
phrases.english: A mourner, during the first two days, is forbidden to put on tefillin.
From the second day, and the second day is included,
he is permitted to put on tefillin;
and if new faces come, he takes them off.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אָבֵל, שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the laws of אבילות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: תפילין from day 3, keep them on for new visitors. רבי יהושע: תפילין from day 2, take them off for new visitors.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole rest of the sugya, which looks for the פסוק behind each opinion.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: the days of mourning for משה
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה explains that רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק about the 'days' of mourning for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? Because it is written: 'And the days of weeping and mourning for משה ended.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה gives the source for רבי אליעזר's view that the main mourning lasts two full days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'days', in the plural, and the smallest plural is two. So the strongest mourning lasts two full days, and תפילין come back on the third.

phrases.english: רב מתנה said:
What is the reason of רבי אליעזר?
As it is written: 'And the days of weeping and mourning for Moses ended.'
phrases.notes: דברים 34:8. 'Days' is plural, so at least two days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first opinion in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Days' (plural) of mourning shows the main mourning is two days

steps.title: רבי יהושע's source: 'a bitter day'
steps.stepSummary: רב עינא explains that רבי יהושע learns from the פסוק 'and its end as a bitter day.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עינא said: What is רבי יהושע's reason? Because it is written: 'And its end as a bitter day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב עינא gives the source for רבי יהושע's view that the main mourning is only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a bitter day', just one. So the strongest mourning is the first day, and תפילין may go back on during the second day.

phrases.english: רב עינא said:
What is the reason of רבי יהושע?
As it is written: 'And its end as a bitter day.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 8:10. 'Day' is singular, so the bitterest mourning is one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עֵינָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second opinion, alongside step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'A bitter day' (singular) shows the main mourning is one day

steps.title: What does רבי יהושע do with the 'days' of mourning for משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע: the פסוק about משה says 'days', which means two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי יהושע too, isn't it written: 'And the days ended'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהושע deals with רבי אליעזר's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה says 'days' of mourning for משה, that seems to prove two days of main mourning. That goes against רבי יהושע, who says only one.

phrases.english: And for רבי יהושע too,
isn't it written: 'And the days ended, etc.'!
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the rest of the פסוק from step 16, about mourning for משה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי אליעזר's פסוק against רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view of one main day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural 'days' in the פסוק about משה suggests two days of main mourning

steps.title: משה was different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע would answer that the mourning for משה was extra strong, so it lasted longer than normal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: משה is different, because the mourning for him was intense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהושע: the פסוק about משה is a special case, not the normal rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people mourned משה more than usual, so his mourning went beyond the normal length. That one case does not set the rule for every אבל.

phrases.english: He would tell you:
Moses is different, because the mourning for him was intense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק about משה sets the normal length of main mourning
steps.terutzMaskana: Mourning for משה was unusually strong, so it teaches nothing about a normal אבל

steps.title: What does רבי אליעזר do with 'a bitter day'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אליעזר: the פסוק says the bitterness is only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for רבי אליעזר too, isn't it written: 'And its end as a bitter day'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns it around and asks how רבי אליעזר deals with רבי יהושע's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A bitter day' sounds like the main mourning is only one day. That seems to go against רבי אליעזר's two days.

phrases.english: And for רבי אליעזר too,
isn't it written: 'And its end as a bitter day'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 18 in the other direction
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view of two main days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The singular 'a bitter day' suggests only one day of main mourning

steps.title: The sharpest bitterness is one day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר would answer that the very worst bitterness is one day, but the strong mourning still lasts two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The main bitterness is one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אליעזר: the פסוק about 'a bitter day' speaks only about the very sharpest pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר agrees the peak bitterness is the first day. But the strong mourning that keeps away תפילין goes for two days, which he learns from משה. So both פסוקים fit his view.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: two main days of mourning (from 'days' for משה), so תפילין on the third day. רבי יהושע: one main day (from 'a bitter day'), so תפילין on the second day. Each side explains the other's פסוק: משה was special, or one day is only the sharpest bitterness.

phrases.english: The main bitterness is one day.
phrases.notes: The very sharpest pain is the first day, but strong mourning still goes for two days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the פסוק as talking only about the peak of the mourning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A bitter day' sets the full length of main mourning at one day
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the sharpest bitterness is one day. The serious mourning period is still two days.

steps.title: עולא rules partly like each תנא
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules like רבי אליעזר about taking off תפילין, and like רבי יהושע about putting them on.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר about taking off the תפילין, and follows רבי יהושע about putting them on.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a practical ruling on the מחלוקת we just learned. He does not pick one side completely. He takes one part from each תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate questions: when the אבל may first put on תפילין, and whether he takes them off when new visitors come. On putting them on, עולא follows רבי יהושע, so the אבל may already wear them on the second day. On taking them off, he follows רבי אליעזר, so the אבל does not need to remove them for new visitors.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
Putting on (here: putting on the תפילין)

steps.whyThisMatters: This split ruling creates a gap. It is not clear what happens on the second day, and that is exactly what the next question asks about.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer regarding removing,
phrases.notes: He means taking off the תפילין when new visitors come to comfort the אבל.

phrases.english: and the halakha follows Rabbi Yehoshua regarding putting on.
phrases.notes: So the אבל may already put on תפילין on the second day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּחֲלִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the מחלוקת from the ברייתא in step 15, whose sources steps 16-21 analyzed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: About removing תפילין, follow רבי אליעזר. About putting them on, follow רבי יהושע, so they may be worn from the second day.

steps.title: Does the אבל take off his תפילין on the second day?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask: according to עולא, if new visitors come on the second day, does the אבל take off his תפילין?
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars asked: On the second day, according to עולא, does he take off the תפילין or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a real question created by עולא's split ruling. The question sets up the next step, where an answer is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא lets the אבל wear תפילין on the second day, like רבי יהושע. But for רבי אליעזר the second day is still a day of strong mourning. So maybe on that day he should take them off when new visitors come. Or maybe עולא's rule of not taking them off applies here too.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
On the second day, according to Ulla,
does he remove or not remove?
phrases.notes: He means: if new visitors come to comfort him that day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a case that עולא's split ruling in step 22 leaves unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, according to עולא, an אבל wearing תפילין on the second day must remove them when new visitors arrive.

steps.title: עולא said he removes them even a hundred times
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from עולא himself: the אבל takes off and puts back on, even a hundred times.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: עולא said, he takes them off and puts them back on, even a hundred times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting another statement of עולא. It shows that on the second day the אבל does take off his תפילין for new visitors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each time new visitors come, he takes the תפילין off. When they leave, he puts them back on. This statement must be about the second day, because on later days עולא already ruled like רבי אליעזר that he does not take them off.

keyTerms.meaning: A hundred times, meaning as often as needed

phrases.english: Come and hear, Ulla said:
He removes and puts on,
phrases.notes: He takes them off when visitors come and puts them back on when they leave.

phrases.english: even a hundred times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the second day he takes the תפילין off for each new group of visitors and puts them back on afterward, even many times.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quoting יהודה בן תימא supports עולא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: יהודה בן תימא says, he takes them off and puts them back on, even a hundred times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports עולא with a ברייתא that says the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא is an אמורא, a later teacher. Here an earlier תנא, יהודה בן תימא, is found saying the same rule. This shows that עולא's position has a source in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this, bringing support

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
Yehuda ben Teima says:
He removes and puts on, even a hundred times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא's statement in step 24 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: עולא's rule that the אבל takes off and puts back on his תפילין, even many times.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting יהודה בן תימא with the same wording.

steps.title: רבא: once he puts them on, he does not take them off
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees: once the אבל has put on his תפילין, he does not take them off again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Once he has put them on, he does not take them off again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different opinion from עולא and יהודה בן תימא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said the אבל takes them off for every new group of visitors. רבא says that once the תפילין are on, they stay on, even if new visitors come.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Once he has put them on,
he does not remove them again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִנִּיחַ שׁוּב אֵינוֹ חוֹלֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the rule of עולא and the ברייתא in steps 24-25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once an אבל puts on תפילין, he does not remove them for new visitors.

steps.title: Challenge: רבא himself ruled like the three-day opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: he ruled elsewhere like the תנא who said three days, so how can he talk about putting on תפילין in these days?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבא himself say: The הלכה follows our תנא, who said three days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's statement using another ruling of his own. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our תנא said the strongest mourning lasts three days, and during that time the אבל does not wear תפילין. If רבא follows that view, the cases discussed here, where the אבל wears them on the second day and new visitors come, should not arise for him. So it looks like רבא contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that, introducing a contradiction
Our תנא, the תנא of our own teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about taking off the תפילין. It asks how רבא can talk about the days when they are worn at all, if he holds that the first three days are without תפילין.

phrases.english: But wasn't it Rava who said:
The halakha follows our Tanna
who said three!
phrases.notes: Three days of the strongest mourning, when the אבל does not put on תפילין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that once the אבל puts on תפילין he does not take them off.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא elsewhere follows the תנא who forbids תפילין for three days. That seems to contradict his discussing an אבל wearing them during the days covered by this מחלוקת.
